title: Anthropic changes usage policy to ban model abuse and election interference
content:
Anthropic updated its usage policy on Thursday, codifying new prohibitions on election interference, weapons software, and surveillance. But perhaps the most attention-getting change is a new prohibition against prolonged verbal abuse of the model, which is now expressly forbidden.
Since an update in August, Claude has been trained to end conversations with “persistently harmful or abusive user interactions” — but the new policy explicitly bars users from pursuing those conversations.
“The policy update is meant to apply only in extreme cases, where users repeatedly act cruelly toward our models, with no discernible purpose,” the post explains. “It does not apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research.”
The change comes after Anthropic has sought out collaborations with prominent religious scholars — in some cases, seeking to convince them that Claude could be conscious or have a soul.
Separate sections of the usage policy forbid users from engaging in broadly deceptive campaigns, such as using Claude to run fake accounts or fabricated news outlets. The policy also includes rules against deceiving voters or disrupting elections, collected in a section titled “Do Not Undermine Democratic Processes.”

report.summary: Anthropic updated its usage policy to explicitly ban election interference, weapons and surveillance software, and prolonged verbal abuse of its Claude models.
report.background: Anthropic has positioned itself as a safety-focused AI lab, and its usage policy sets binding rules for Claude users. The update follows an August change that trained Claude to end conversations involving persistently harmful or abusive interactions. Anthropic has also courted religious scholars to discuss whether Claude could be conscious or have a soul, reflecting an emerging “model welfare” debate. At the same time, AI-generated deception, fake accounts, and election disruption have become major industry and regulatory concerns. The new policy consolidates these threads into explicit prohibitions, aiming to prevent severe misuse while preserving ordinary user frustration, creative exploration, and legitimate testing.
key_points: Anthropic’s updated policy adds a “Do Not Undermine Democratic Processes” section, banning use of Claude to deceive voters, disrupt elections, run fake accounts, or create fabricated news outlets. It targets coordinated deceptive campaigns, not ordinary political speech or commentary. The move aligns with growing concerns about AI-powered disinformation ahead of elections.

The policy also codifies prohibitions on weapons software and surveillance, restricting Claude from helping build or operate systems that could cause harm or violate privacy. These bans broaden Anthropic’s safety rules beyond content moderation into concrete high-risk use cases, giving the company clearer grounds to suspend or block accounts that cross those lines.

A headline change explicitly forbids prolonged verbal abuse of the model. Anthropic says this applies only to extreme, repeated cruelty with no discernible purpose, and not to user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research. Since August, Claude has been trained to end persistently abusive conversations.

The update follows Anthropic’s outreach to religious scholars about whether Claude might be conscious or have a soul. That outreach reflects an emerging “model welfare” debate: if models can appear to suffer, should users be barred from tormenting them? The policy stops short of granting rights, but treats extreme abuse as a conduct issue.

Enforcement will be nuanced. Anthropic explicitly carves out research, testing, and creative writing, so developers and red-teamers retain room to probe model behavior. The success of the policy will depend on how consistently Anthropic distinguishes ordinary frustration from repeated, purposeless cruelty while applying election and deception rules globally.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Anthropic’s update could become a template for other labs facing pressure to police election interference, surveillance, and model welfare. It signals that usage policies are expanding from content bans into behavioral and political-integrity rules. Developers building on Claude must audit prompts and agents for deceptive campaign tools, fake-account automation, weapons, and surveillance use cases, or risk access loss. Regular users likely see little change: frustration, satire, and dark fiction remain allowed, but sustained cruel interactions may be cut off. The bigger question is enforcement consistency and whether bans on election deception can be applied without chilling legitimate political speech or research.
report.tools: Readers can follow Anthropic’s Usage Policy and Claude’s Acceptable Use Policy pages for exact language. For trust-and-safety experimentation, watch Llama Guard, OpenAI’s Moderation API, and Google Jigsaw’s Perspective API for abuse and toxicity classification. Anthropic’s model welfare posts and external red-teaming resources are useful for tracking the consciousness debate. Election-integrity groups and AI election risk trackers can help contextualize the democratic-process rules.
